It is a Meccan surah.

It has already been reported from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite "Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la" (Surah al-A'la) and "al-Ghashiyah" during the 'Eid prayer and on Friday.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 88, verses 17–26:

He, exalted is He, says, commanding His servants to reflect on His creatures, which indicate His power and greatness: ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ For it is a wondrous creation, and its composition is remarkable. It is extremely strong and powerful, yet it yields to carrying heavy loads, submits to a weak handler, is eaten, its wool is used, and its milk is drunk. They were directed to this because the camel was the most common of the Arabs' riding and carrying animals. Shurayh the judge used to say: "Come out with us, so that we may look at the camels, how they were created, and at the sky, how it was raised?" That is, how Allah, mighty and majestic, raised it from the earth to this great height, as He says: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts?﴾ [Qaf: 6]

﴿And at the mountains, how they were set up﴾, that is, made firmly erected, fixed and established, so that the earth would not shake with its inhabitants, and He placed in them what He placed of benefits and minerals.

﴿And at the earth, how it was spread out?﴾ That is, how it was spread, stretched and made smooth. Thus He directed the Bedouin to draw proof from what he observes: his camel on which he rides, the sky above his head, the mountain before him, and the earth beneath him, toward the power of the Creator and Maker of these things, and that He is the great Lord, the Creator, the Disposer, the Owner, and that He is the God who alone deserves worship besides whom there is none.

Thus Dimam swore in his question to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as related by Imam Ahmad, where he said:

Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughira related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: "We were forbidden to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about anything, and it pleased us that a sensible man from the Bedouin would come and ask him while we listened. A man from the Bedouin came and said: 'O Muhammad, your messenger came to us and claimed that you assert that Allah sent you.' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' He said: 'Who created the sky?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who created the earth?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who set up these mountains and placed in them what He placed?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'By the One who created the sky and the earth and set up these mountains, has Allah sent you?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Your messenger claimed that five prayers are obligatory upon us in our day and night.' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' He said: 'By the One who sent you, has Allah commanded you with this?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Your messenger claimed that zakat is obligatory upon us in our wealth?' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' He said: 'By the One who sent you, has Allah commanded you with this?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Your messenger claimed that the pilgrimage to the House is obligatory upon those who are able to make their way to it.' He said: 'He spoke the truth.' Then he turned away and said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I will neither add to these nor subtract anything from them.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If he is truthful, he will surely enter Paradise.'"

Muslim related it from Amr al-Naqid, from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, with the same chain [al-Musnad (3/143) and Sahih Muslim, no. 12]. Al-Bukhari recorded it in suspended form (ta'liq). At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari (1/148) with Fath, Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. 619, and al-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. 2401]. Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id al-Maqbari, from Shurayk ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Namir, from Anas, with the same chain, in full [al-Musnad (3/168), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 63, Sunan Abi Dawud no. 486, al-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. 2402, and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 1402]. At its end it says: "I am Dimam ibn Tha'laba, brother of the Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr."

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Ishaq related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ja'far related to us, Abd Allah ibn Dinar related to me, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) often used to narrate about a woman in the Jahiliyya who was on the top of a mountain with a son of hers who was tending sheep. Her son said to her: 'O mother, who created you?' She said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who created my father?' She said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who created me?' She said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who created the sky?' She said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who created the earth?' She said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who created the mountain?' She said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who created these sheep?' She said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Indeed I hear that Allah has a great matter.' And he threw himself from the mountain and was cut to pieces."

Ibn Umar said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) often used to tell us this."

Ibn Dinar said: "Ibn Umar often used to tell us this."

[Ibn Adi related it in al-Kamil (4/178) from Abu Ya'la with the same wording, and said: "It is not preserved; no one narrates it from Ibn Dinar except Abd Allah ibn Ja'far."]

There is weakness in its chain. This Abd Allah ibn Ja'far is al-Madini, whom his son, the Imam Ali ibn al-Madini, and others declared weak.

And His saying: ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller﴾. That is: remind them, O Muhammad, of what you were sent with to them, for upon you is only the conveying, and upon Us is the reckoning. For this reason He said: ﴿You are not over them a controller.﴾ Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: "You are not over them a tyrant."

Ibn Zayd said: "You are not one who compels them to faith."

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: 'There is no god but Allah.' When they say it, they have protected their blood and their property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is upon Allah, mighty and majestic." Then he recited: ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller.﴾

Thus Muslim related it in the Book of Faith (al-Iman), and at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i in the Books of Tafsir of their Sunan, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, with this addition [al-Musnad (3/300), Sahih Muslim no. 21, Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. 3341, and al-Sunan al-Kubra of an-Nasa'i no. 11670]. This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Hurayra without mention of this verse [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2946 and Sahih Muslim no. 21].

* *

And His saying: ﴿except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾. That is: he turns away from acting by its pillars, and disbelieves in the truth in his heart and tongue. This is like His saying: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 31–32]. For this reason He said: ﴿Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.﴾ Imam Ahmad said:

Qutayba related to us, Layth related to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Ali ibn Khalid [in A: "Ali ibn Abi Khalid", and the reading here follows M and the Musnad], that Abu Umama al-Bahili passed by Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Mu'awiya and asked him about the gentlest word he had heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Does not every one of you enter Paradise, except one who runs away from Allah like a camel runs away from its people.'"

Imam Ahmad alone recorded it [al-Musnad (5/258)]. This Ali ibn Khalid was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim from his father, and he added nothing to what is here except: "He related from Abu Umama, and from him Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal" [al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil (6/184)]. Al-Haythami in al-Majma' (10/403) said: "He is trustworthy."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾, that is, their place of return and their turning back. ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾, that is, We will call them to account for their deeds and recompense them for them: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Ghashiyah, and all praise and grace belong to Allah.
